title: Strawberry Granola with Pumpkin Seeds and Coconut
changes_from_base: Smaller batch with honey and sugar heated together with oil and a touch of chilli; freeze-dried strawberries are stirred in at the end so they stay crisp and colour the granola pink.
summary: A strawberry granola with pumpkin seeds and toasted almonds, finished with freeze-dried strawberry pieces that add tartness and natural sweetness, lovely with yoghurt.
equipment: large rimmed baking tray (about 33 x 46 cm)

ingredients.item: almonds (or hazelnuts or cashews), roughly chopped
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Get the oven going at 150 °C (130 °C fan); put a sheet of baking paper on a large rimmed baking tray.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: In a large bowl, combine 200 g rolled oats, 100 g almonds (or hazelnuts or cashews) roughly chopped, 40 g unsweetened coconut chips (optional) and 70 g pumpkin seeds.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Warm 70 g runny honey, 40 g light brown sugar, 60 ml coconut (or olive) oil, ⅛ tsp chilli flakes (optional) and ½ tsp fine salt in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring, until the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Tip the warm dressing over the oat mixture and stir thoroughly until everything is evenly coated.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Spread on the tray and bake for 15 min, stir, then bake for 20-25 min more until golden.

steps.title: Add
steps.text: Once completely cold, stir through 20 g freeze-dried strawberries, crushing some into a fine pink powder.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Keep in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

tips: Toast the granola twice—once for 15 minutes, then again for 20-25 minutes—to achieve even browning
Crush some freeze-dried strawberries into powder so they distribute throughout the granola
The optional chilli flakes add subtle warmth that complements the strawberry flavour beautifully
storage: Keep in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
